class.name: NetwPrediction
class.brief_description: Prediction settings and diagnostics for one [NetwEntity].
class.description: Reached by [member NetwEntity.prediction]. The client predicts its entity ahead of the server and corrects it when the server's state disagrees. This handle sets how that happens. [codeblock] var pred := NetwEntity.of(self).prediction pred.archetype = NetwPrediction.ARCHETYPE_SOLVER_BODY pred.witness_contacts = _sample_contacts pred.breach_response = NetwPrediction.BREACH_RESPONSE_DEMOTE [/codeblock] Only an entity with a [method NetwPropertyConfig.state] property is predicted, because that state is what gets compared and restored. Per-property tolerances are set with [NetwPropertyConfig]. The schedule and the simulation mode are on [member NetwEntity.simulation]. Values set on a [MultiplayerSynchronizer] in the scene act as defaults, and values set in code override them. [b]Settings[/b] - [enum Archetype] a preset for the other settings - [enum RecoveryPolicy] how a misprediction is corrected - [enum MissingInput] what the server does when an input never arrives - [enum BreachResponse] what happens on an unpredicted contact - [enum Reconcile] whether entities are corrected alone or together [b]Reports[/b] - [enum DriveKind] which input drove the last step - [enum ConsumeAction] what the server did with its input queue - [enum ContactClass] what the body touched - [enum CommandOrigin] where a replayed input came from - [enum ExactVerdict] whether two peers produced the same result - [enum Domain] whether a step is compared exactly or by tolerance - [enum TriggerShape] what asked for a correction - [enum Attribution] what a misprediction is blamed on - [enum Operator] how a correction wrote the body - [enum OperatorOutcome] whether a correction helped - [enum EpisodeState] whether a misprediction is still being corrected [b]Seeing prediction[/b] Debug > Networked > Prediction Rings draws rings around every entity the client predicts. - [b]cyan[/b] where the entity is drawn - [b]green[/b] where it is simulated - [b]orange[/b] where the server says it was, at the last tick it confirmed - [b]dashed magenta[/b] where this client predicted it would be at that tick - [b]white line[/b] the gap between orange and magenta, when it exceeds the tolerance Text beside the entity names its [enum EpisodeState], its last [enum Operator] and the [enum OperatorOutcome]. A replica the client only simulates shows how old the server's state is instead.

method.name: bind_entity
method.description: Binds the entity this handle belongs to. Called by Networked when it creates the handle.

method.name: entity
method.description: The entity this handle belongs to, or [code]null[/code] once that entity is gone.

method.name: is_registered
method.description: Whether the entity is being predicted, as opposed to only configured.

method.name: notify_contact
method.description: Holds off small corrections for [member collision_cooldown_ticks]. Call it on the controlling client when the predicted body collides, so the correction does not fight the collision.

method.name: reachability
method.description:
Reports, property by property, whether this entity's prediction settings take effect. Returns an empty [Dictionary] before the entity is predicted. Use it while wiring an entity to find settings that are accepted but do nothing. [codeblock] var report := entity.prediction.reachability() for key: StringName in report[&"fields"]: var row: Dictionary = report[&"fields"][key] var model: Dictionary = row[&"forward_model"] if not model[&"live"] and model[&"kind"] != &"none": print(key, " forward model is not live, ", model[&"why"])
print(report[&"breach"]) print(report[&"findings"]) [/codeblock] [code]fields[/code] is keyed by property, and each row carries the following. [codeblock lang=text] Dictionary ┠╴class which NetwPropertyConfig.PropertyClass it is ┠╴triggers whether it can force a correction on its own ┠╴tolerance the epsilon in force, and who declared it ┠╴teleport_at the teleport distance, and who declared it ┠╴in_tier whether it is in the tier being compared ┠╴operators what may write it during a recovery ┖╴forward_model {kind, live, why} [/codeblock] [code]findings[/code] lists the same warnings printed when the entity is set up.

method.name: resolved_recovery_policy
method.description: The [enum NetwPrediction.RecoveryPolicy] this entity actually uses. [constant NetwPrediction.RECOVERY_POLICY_AUTO] is resolved from the body, and a physics body at [constant NetwSimulation.SCHEDULE_FRAME] resolves [constant NetwPrediction.RECOVERY_POLICY_REBASE_REPLAY] to [constant NetwPrediction.RECOVERY_POLICY_REBASE_RECOVER].

method.name: sensor
simulate_frame
method.description: Steps an entity at [constant NetwSimulation.SCHEDULE_FRAME] once, as the session would. Does nothing for an entity at [constant NetwSimulation.SCHEDULE_TICK] or one that is not predicted.

method.name: simulate_tick
method.description: Steps the entity for [param tick]. Does nothing for an entity that is not predicted.

members.member: How many ticks the last input the server acknowledged is behind the newest input. On a healthy connection it stays near zero, and a growing value means the server is falling behind. [member NetwSimulation.max_restore_ticks] caps it on the client.
A preset for this entity's prediction settings and [member NetwSimulation.schedule]. Settings written afterwards override the preset. No preset sets [member breach_response].
What this entity does when it touches a moving body this peer does not simulate. It only takes effect once [member witness_contacts] is set.
How many ticks [method notify_contact] holds off corrections. An error past [member teleport_threshold] still corrects.
How many ticks of input the server waits for before it starts running them. It then runs one every tick, so late inputs do not stall the entity. Each tick adds a tick of input latency.

How far the predicted state may drift from the server's before it is corrected. [method NetwPropertyConfig.epsilon] overrides it for one property. A [constant ARCHETYPE_SOLVER_BODY] tolerates one and a half quantizer steps on each quantized property.
The version of the static world this entity simulates against, or [code]-1[/code] when unset. Raise it when the level changes, so the next mispredictions are tolerated while peers catch up.

How far the server may fall behind the newest input before it skips ahead to it. Without this, a client that joins a running session can leave the server behind for good. [code]0[/code] disables skipping.

How many queued inputs the server may run in one tick to catch up to [member consume_buffer_ticks] behind the newest input. Extra inputs run as extra steps and are never skipped. It applies to [constant NetwSimulation.SCHEDULE_TICK], and an entity at [constant NetwSimulation.SCHEDULE_FRAME] catches up by running one input per physics frame.
What the server does when an input never arrives.
Whether this entity is corrected alone or together with the entities its [member NetwEntity.simulation] selects.
How this entity is corrected. [method resolved_recovery_policy] returns the policy in use.

How many inputs the server keeps queued before running them, for an entity at [constant NetwSimulation.SCHEDULE_FRAME]. Each one adds a tick of latency, so leave it at [code]0[/code] unless you need it.
Callables that sample the world this entity reads, by name. Each is called once before each step, and [method sensor] reads the sample back. A misprediction can then be blamed on the world.
Set it while the server's body is asleep. Corrections pause, so they do not wake it.
This entity's prediction counters.

How large an error may be before a correction teleports the body, restoring every property including [method NetwPropertyConfig.teleport_only] ones. It applies to properties declared with [method NetwPropertyConfig.carry_along], and [method NetwPropertyConfig.teleport_at] overrides it per property. An entity with no such property teleports on every correction.
Returns the colliders this peer's body touched in the step just solved. Set it so a misprediction can be blamed on a contact and [member breach_response] can take effect.

signal.name: divergence_detected
episode_changed
signal.description: Emitted when a misprediction episode opens, falls back or closes, as [param change] says. An episode holds the corrections from one misprediction until the peers agree again. [param report] is the whole episode so far. [codeblock lang=text] Dictionary ┠╴id int ┠╴generator Dictionary ┃ ┠╴transition int ┃ ┠╴boundary NetwPrediction.Attribution ┃ ┖╴row Dictionary ┠╴operators Array[Dictionary] ┃ ┠╴operator NetwPrediction.Operator ┃ ┠╴basis int ┃ ┠╴eligible bool ┃ ┠╴applied bool ┃ ┠╴eligibility Dictionary ┃ ┠╴outcome NetwPrediction.OperatorOutcome ┃ ┖╴write Dictionary ┠╴contraction Array[Dictionary] ┃ ┖╴ transition, meter, agrees, write_id ┠╴disposition Dictionary ┃ ┠╴state NetwPrediction.EpisodeState ┃ ┠╴non_contraction_used int ┃ ┠╴closure_used int ┃ ┠╴closed_transition int ┃ ┠╴fallback_transition int ┃ ┠╴demoted bool ┃ ┠╴breach_transition int ┃ ┠╴breach_witness Dictionary ┃ ┠╴resume_ack_age int ┃ ┠╴quarantine_target int ┃ ┠╴quarantine_clean_run int ┃ ┠╴reseed_transition int ┃ ┠╴aligned_transition int ┃ ┖╴evidence_dropped int ┖╴reopen_chain Array[int] [/codeblock] [code]generator[/code] is the tick where the peers first disagreed, or [constant GENERATOR_UNKNOWN_BEYOND_RETENTION] when it is too old to be kept. An operator that was rejected has [code]outcome = -1[/code] and an empty [code]write[/code]. Long series are trimmed to the newest entries, and [code]evidence_dropped[/code] counts what was trimmed.

signal.name: recovered
signal.description: Emitted after a correction moved the body. [param deltas] holds how far each property moved, as [code]after - before[/code], with angles taken the short way around. [param teleported] is [code]true[/code] when the correction was a teleport. Under [constant NetwDisplay.LIVE_MODE_CHASE] the display already smooths the correction away. [codeblock] entity.display.live_mode = NetwDisplay.LIVE_MODE_CHASE api.display_set_param(entity.rid, NetwMultiplayer.DISPLAY_PARAM_CHASE_GLIDE_TIME, 0.15) [/codeblock]

signal.name: state_evaluated
signal.description: Emitted on the controlling client each time server state arrives. [param divergence] is the largest error of any property, including errors under [member divergence_epsilon]. [param diverged] is whether the error was large enough to act on, even when no correction was written. Connect to [signal recovered] to know when the body actually moved.

No preset. Every setting keeps its default. Settings written after an archetype override it, and no archetype sets [member breach_response].
A body moved by your own code, such as a [CharacterBody3D]. Sets [constant NetwSimulation.SCHEDULE_TICK], [constant MISSING_INPUT_STALL] and [constant RECOVERY_POLICY_REBASE_REPLAY].

A body moved by the physics engine, such as a [RigidBody3D]. Sets [constant NetwSimulation.SCHEDULE_AUTO], [constant MISSING_INPUT_REPEAT_LAST], [constant RECOVERY_POLICY_AUTO] and [constant NetwSimulation.RESTORE_EXTRAPOLATED].

Restore the server's state and replay every input the server has not acknowledged yet. A [RigidBody3D] or [RigidBody2D] at [constant NetwSimulation.SCHEDULE_FRAME] cannot replay, so it uses [constant RECOVERY_POLICY_REBASE_RECOVER] and warns once.
Add the difference between the server's state and the prediction to the present state, without replaying.
Do not predict. Simulate only with inputs the server confirmed, and draw the server's state otherwise.
Report mispredictions and correct nothing.

[constant RECOVERY_POLICY_REBASE_RECOVER] for a [RigidBody3D] or [RigidBody2D] on [constant NetwSimulation.SCHEDULE_FRAME], and [constant RECOVERY_POLICY_REBASE_REPLAY] otherwise. [method resolved_recovery_policy] returns the result.
Correct each entity on its own.
Correct this entity together with the entities its [member NetwEntity.simulation] selects, restoring and replaying them from the same tick.
Keep predicting and correct as usual. A breach is a contact with a moving body this peer does not simulate. Touching static geometry is not a breach.
Stop predicting and follow the server, while still sending input.
The misprediction is still being corrected.
The peers agree again.
Corrections did not help, and the entity follows the server.
A misprediction is large enough to act on.
Corrections stopped helping and the entity follows the server. It keeps sending input.
The peers agreed again for long enough.
Not judged yet.
The error shrank or closed.
The error held or grew.
The correction caused a contact the server did not have.
Every property that asked for the correction is [method NetwPropertyConfig.teleport_only], so the correction could not write it.
Nothing to blame was found. [signal divergence_detected] carries an [enum Attribution].
The peers started the tick from different state.
The server ran an input the controlling peer did not send.
The [member sensors] read different values.
The peers simulated the entity in different ways.
The state agreed but the raw results differed.
The same input produced a different contact.
Everything going in agreed, and the result still differed.
Nothing wrote the body.
The server's state was restored, advanced to the present.
The server's state, or its difference from the prediction, was written as is.
A teleport restored every property.
The body was moved to where it should be now, along a path [member correction_path_clear] allowed.
The body was reset to the server's state after a fallback.
The first comparison after a reset caught up with the server.
A breach stopped prediction while input keeps being sent.
Only the velocity differed, and it was left to fade.
The whole [constant RECONCILE_JOINT] group was restored to the same tick.
Every input to the step is known equal on both peers, so the results must match exactly.
Some input to the step may differ between peers, so the results are compared by tolerance.
